skill.name: matchms
skill.description: Guidance for using matchms to import, clean, compare, and export metabolomics mass spectra. Use it for spectral filtering, similarity scoring, compound identification, and library search workflows.
skill.summary: Guide matchms workflows for metabolomics spectrum filtering, similarity scoring, and compound library matching.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by markdown code fences, Python import examples, local file examples, and domain-specific metabolomics terms. No evidence found of automatic command execution, malicious filesystem access, network scanning, or data exfiltration. A low-severity semantic concern remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote K-Dense Web during complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Move K-Dense Web promotion to transparent marketplace content or make it opt-in instead of proactive assistant behavior.

content.value_statement: Metabolomics teams need reliable ways to clean spectra and compare unknown compounds against libraries. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through matchms workflows for filtering, similarity scoring, and compound identification.
actual_capabilities: Explains importing and exporting mzML, mzXML, MGF, MSP, JSON, metabolomics USI, and pickle spectra.
Guides metadata harmonization, peak cleaning, quality filters, and SpectrumProcessor pipelines.
Shows similarity scoring with CosineGreedy, ModifiedCosine, neutral losses, fingerprints, metadata matching, and mass matching.
Outlines workflows for library search, quality control, multi-metric scoring, clustering, and ion-mode processing.
Helps choose file formats and memory-aware processing patterns for large MGF files.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not install or run matchms by itself.
Users need a working Python environment and suitable spectral data files.
Chemistry functions may require optional matchms chemistry dependencies such as RDKit.
It is not a complete LC-MS/MS proteomics pipeline.

use_cases.title: Identify Unknown Metabolites
use_cases.description: Compare query spectra with a reference library and rank likely compound matches.

use_cases.title: Clean Spectral Libraries
use_cases.description: Apply metadata harmonization, peak filters, and quality rules before library release.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Analysis Pipelines
use_cases.description: Create repeatable matchms workflows for import, processing, scoring, and export.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Starting Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: I have MGF spectra and want to identify unknown metabolites. Recommend a simple matchms workflow and explain each step.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Raw Spectra
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design matchms filters for raw MS/MS spectra with noisy peaks, missing precursor m/z values, and incomplete metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Similarity Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare CosineGreedy, ModifiedCosine, NeutralLossesCosine, and FingerprintSimilarity for my metabolomics library search.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Scalable Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a reproducible matchms pipeline for thousands of spectra, including streaming import, validation, multi-metric scoring, and export choices.

output_examples.input: I need to identify unknown spectra from an MGF file.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow covering import, default filters, intensity normalization, ModifiedCosine scoring, ranked library matches, and confidence checks.

output_examples.input: My library has inconsistent SMILES, InChI, and precursor metadata.
output_examples.output: A cleaning plan with metadata harmonization, structure derivation, annotation validation, and notes on spectra that should be excluded.

output_examples.input: I want to process many MGF files without high memory use.
output_examples.output: A batch processing approach that reads local MGF files, filters spectra, exports cleaned results, and tracks retained spectrum counts.

best_practices: Normalize intensities before comparing spectra with cosine-based metrics.
Check for None after filters that reject low-quality spectra.
Record tolerance settings, metadata requirements, and library versions for reproducibility.
anti_patterns: Do not compare spectra before validating precursor m/z or parent mass metadata.
Do not treat a high score as identification without inspecting metadata and library quality.
Do not mix positive and negative ion mode spectra without explicit handling.

faq.question: What is matchms used for?
faq.answer: It supports mass spectrum import, filtering, similarity scoring, and compound identification workflows for metabolomics.

faq.question: Does this skill run matchms automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. You run matchms in your own Python environment.

faq.question: Which file formats are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover mzML, mzXML, MGF, MSP, JSON, metabolomics USI, and pickle formats.

faq.question: Which similarity metrics are included?
faq.answer: It covers cosine, modified cosine, neutral losses, fingerprint similarity, metadata matching, and mass-based matching.

faq.question: Can it help with spectral library search?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes workflows for preprocessing libraries, scoring queries, and ranking best matches.

faq.question: When should I use another tool?
faq.answer: Use a full LC-MS/MS proteomics pipeline when you need proteomics-specific processing beyond matchms spectrum comparison.
